![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226602/assets/caabcee019c7e97355b6a30f820872207e3f43245d97d3d09a44bf400628a975.png)

Find the polar coordinates of the intersection points of the polar curves $r=3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ and $r=4+3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ shown above. Round your answers to $1$ decimal place where appropriate.
question.worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$  

$$
\{\begin{aligned}r=3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ r=4+3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solve for $\theta .$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =4+3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =-1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[{0}^{∘},{360}^{∘}),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}≈{191.5}^{∘}$ and ${\theta }_{2}≈348.5,$ rounded to $1$ decimal place. 

Now, we use the equation $r=4+3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ to find the $r$-coordinates of the intersection points: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1} & =4+3\operatorname{sin}⁡{\theta }_{1}=4+3\cdot (-\frac{1}{5})=\frac{17}{5}=3.4 \\ {r}_{2} & =4+3\operatorname{cos}⁡{\theta }_{2}=4+3\cdot (-\frac{1}{5})=\frac{17}{5}=3.4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, polar coordinates of the points of intersection are

$\,$ $(r,\theta )≈(3.4,{191.5}^{∘})\,$ and $\,(r,\theta )≈(3.4,{348.5}^{∘}).$
